To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
curvilinearily is evaluated by a moving 4-dot window that evaluates collinearity, smoothness, and spacing.

the probability distribution of inter-dot angles is a gaussian with a negative correlation, that the correlation is predicted by the probability distribution of the generating process, and that the probability distribution is consistent with a 4-dot moving window.

the perception of a curvilinear pattern can be regarded as the outcome of a probabilistic inference, and that the inference can be modeled in terms of a gaussian distribution of successive inter-angle differences.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the visual system evaluates a chain of dots as having been generated from a curvilinear process.
the role of probabilistic inference in visual pattern recognition.
the role of covariation in the perceptual grouping of visual elements into a curve.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

curvilinear perception is a kind of probabilism in which the perceptual system is sensitive to the joint probability distribution of successive angles, and is also sensitive to the spacing of the dots along the virtual generating curve.

the perception of curvilinears is a kind of probabilistically based inference, in which a curvilinear pattern is regarded as a kind more likely than chance, given the observed inter-dot angles, but the inference is limited by a window of 4-5 dots.

subjects' judgments of curvilinear regularity depend on the joint distribution of inter-dot angles, and that this distribution is a function of a moving, 4-dot window, with a negative correlation coefficient of approximately -.5.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
subjects' judgments of curvilinear regularity are sensitive to the joint distribution of the angles between successive dots.
the percept of curvilinearty is a kind of probabilistically weighted inference over a local window, and that the weighting is sensitive to both the mean and the covariance structure.
the perceptual system is able to detect a curvilinear structure in a chain of dots, and that this structure can be described in terms of a simple probabilistic model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
perceptual grouping can be regarded as the product of a series of probabilistic inference steps.
the human visual system is sensitive to the covariance between successive angles in a chain of dots, but insensitive to the covariance between non-successive ones.
the perception of curvilinearily involves the computation of a covariance matrix.
